name: Spider Plant
description: Spider Plant (Chlorophytum spp.) is considered non-toxic to cats and is safe for them to be around. The ASPCA lists it as non-toxic, and it contains no known toxic principle. Many cats are simply attracted to its dangling leaves and like to bat at or chew on them. While the plant itself is not poisonous, eating a large amount of the fibrous leaves can occasionally cause mild stomach upset, such as vomiting or diarrhea. The effects are generally self-limiting and do not require medical treatment. If you notice your cat is eating the plant frequently or showing signs of discomfort, it is best to move the plant to a location where they cannot reach it.

symptoms.name: Mild nausea or digestive upset (which may include vomiting)
symptoms.notes: This is a rare and mild physical reaction to consuming heavy amounts of fibrous plant material, not a toxicological reaction6. No veterinary action is needed unless the digestive upset is prolonged or the cat begins to show other unusual behaviors.
